## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kassapabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 26) constitutes the twenty-sixth chapter of the canonical *Buddhavaṁsa*, situated within the late strata of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Bearing the title translated as *The History of the Buddha Kassapa*, the text delivers the biographical verse chronicle of Kassapa, the twenty-fourth past Buddha of the lineage and the immediate predecessor to Gotama Buddha [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral lists no independent curated parallels in early Buddhist literature, computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread internal textual reuse across Pali literature, registering 459 matching passages across 32 separate texts [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The closest Pali reuses occur with the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā* (148 matches), as well as with narrative and doctrinal expositions in the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Thūpavaṁsa* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, the work shares dense formulaic verse sequences with other biographical chapters within the *Buddhavaṁsa*, particularly the accounts of Vipassī (Bv 21), Koṇḍañña (Bv 4), Kakusandha (Bv 24), Sikhī (Bv 22), and Koṇāgamana (Bv 25) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects significant textual correspondence with the Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (with similarity scores up to 85) and the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032), alongside minor matches with works such as the *Pitāputrasamāgamasūtra* and the *Saptabuddhānvayamaṅgalagāthā* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
